description: :name bind-variable references inside the PLAIN SQL statements of a Snowflake Scripting block - INSERT VALUES, WHERE predicates, UPDATE SET and arbitrary expressions - resolved from the block's procedural scope, a stored procedure's PARAMETERS included. These previously failed at parse time ('bind variable not ported'); only the bare-name form worked. A declared-but-unset variable resolves to NULL rather than erroring, while an UNDECLARED one is an error and not a silent NULL - and live does not call that a bind-variable problem at all: it reports the NAME as an unresolvable identifier, at the COLON's offset. That offset rule is measured across four statement families (INSERT VALUES, UPDATE SET, UPDATE WHERE, DELETE WHERE) and the position is the colon every time. SELECT :1 is grammar-accepted as a numeric bind and, unbound, reports the missing bind rather than a syntax error. The last test is the parser boundary that goes with all this: a variant PATH step may be a KEYWORD the grammar admits as an identifier, and the colon before it is still path syntax and not a bind - so src:value:attributes:core.x reads the nested field instead of refusing ':core' as a dotted bind. Converted 1:1 from scripting/BindVariableDmlTest (now retired); the Java computed each expected offset with sql.indexOf(':nope') so the claim was the RULE rather than four transcribed numbers - the converted steps carry the four numbers that rule produces (32, 24, 39, 32) beside the statements they come from.

steps.sql: DECLARE v VARCHAR DEFAULT 'hello'; BEGIN INSERT INTO t VALUES (:v); RETURN 'ok'; END
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE log_it(v VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO call_log VALUES (:v); RETURN 'logged'; END $$
DECLARE x INTEGER DEFAULT 2; BEGIN DELETE FROM nums WHERE n = :x; RETURN 'ok'; END
SELECT n FROM nums ORDER BY n
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
DECLARE nv VARCHAR DEFAULT 'new'; BEGIN UPDATE t SET s = :nv WHERE id = 1; RETURN 'ok'; END
SELECT s FROM t ORDER BY id
DECLARE x INTEGER DEFAULT 41; BEGIN INSERT INTO t VALUES (:x + 1); RETURN 'ok'; END
DECLARE v VARCHAR; BEGIN INSERT INTO t VALUES (:v); RETURN 'ok'; END
BEGIN INSERT INTO t VALUES (:nope); RETURN 'ok'; END
